description:
Search EVE Online public contracts by what is inside them - blueprint ME/TE/runs, abyssal module rolls, and multi-item pack appraisal against Jita prices.


Fixed
- MutaMarket estimates are back. Every abyssal module read as unpriced, the
  estimate showing a dash and the appraisal footnote blaming MutaMarket for it.
  MutaMarket rebuilt their site in early September and the module moved one
  level down in their reply, while we went on reading the old level. A reply we can't
  read now retries the next time you open the contract, instead of being
  remembered as an unpriced roll for six hours.
- The unpriced-lines note no longer blames MutaMarket for a roll it was never
  asked about. "Rolls MutaMarket hasn't priced" is their answer; a lookup that
  failed now says so in its own words, and the estimate's tooltip says it too.
  That sentence is what made the outage above look like an ordinary quiet day.
- Estimates remembered during the outage are not trusted after the update.
  Anything looked up while the reading was broken was stored as "no price", and
  it would have kept saying so for up to six hours after you updated. Contracts
  you opened recently are asked about again instead.

Changed
- A price source that answers with nothing is treated as unavailable rather
  than as free items. Fuzzwork replies about every item it is asked, so a
  reply naming none of them is one we could not read: those prices now come from
  EVE's own order books, the way they already do when Fuzzwork is down.
- A snapshot missing a column we read is refused, with the reason. Refresh
  used to load it and leave the column blank everywhere, so a renamed field
  upstream would quietly empty the blueprint search instead of failing. The
  previous snapshot stays loaded and readable, and a refresh can be retried.

Neither the macOS nor the Windows build is code-signed - that needs a paid
certificate - so the first launch takes one extra step. macOS: open it,
Done, then System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. Windows:
More info → Run anyway. Linux: chmod +x the AppImage (some distros
also need FUSE).
After that the app updates itself from this page: every build is minisign-signed
and the updater checks that signature before replacing anything. The .sig
files and latest.json are what makes that work - you don't need to download
them.
